name: graph_apply
title: Apply a query patch or a batch of bundles
description: Create, patch or delete stored records (entities) and their named groups of fields (components) in one atomic transaction: the whole batch is accepted or refused. `bundles` is an array of bundles, each one entity as {entity: {eid}, <component>: {<properties>}}, the shape a client's apply() takes. An omitted property is unchanged, a null property is cleared, a null component is removed, and $delete: true deletes the entity. Every bundle names its entity but an edge: a new entity's eid is '$name', a name of your own, one per entity (the same '$name' twice in a batch is one entity, and a reference to it anywhere in the batch points at it); the graph makes the eid, and the result gives it beside the '$alias' you used. An edge's eid is made from its ends, so an edge bundle needs no entity: {edge: {from, to}, <relation>: {}}. An existing entity is its eid (an entity's unique string id) or name. Where this store keeps names, alias: {name: '<your name>'} beside a '$name' eid makes the write idempotent: the same name again patches the entity holding it, and a name works wherever an eid does. $was: {doc: {body: "<hash>"}} states what a read-modify-write was based on: per component and property, the SHA-256 of the value you read (null for none); if one has changed since, the whole batch is refused, naming the property and its current value. That is compare-and-set: of two callers spending the same balance, only one succeeds. The result is the transaction as applied, one bundle per entity: {entity: {eid, num}}, every component as written, the stamps added (created, updated) and the '$alias' you used; each deleted entity, consequences included, is {entity, tombstone: {}} alone. graph_schema reads the components and properties this store declares; the server refuses one nobody declared. check: true is a dry run: every check is made and the transaction rolled back, answering what a kept write would (each '$name' resolved) or its exact refusal, which is how a plan of several entities and their edges is proven before any of it is written. A check's answer ends 'Checked: nothing was written', and its eids are the check's alone: the write makes its own, so send the same '$name's again rather than the eids a check showed. With secret{name, value}, an optional doc{title, body} in the same bundle can say what the secret is for and who uses it; never put a credential or vault handle there. Documentation: https://yaks.app/docs/store. Alternatively, q writes one entity using the shared query grammar: '.entity.eid=<id> .book.pages=500' or '<id> .book.pages=500'. Values follow the property's schema: numbers and booleans become those types; text, references and enum values stay strings. The scalar null clears a property (quoted null also clears); .component adds it and !component removes it. The target is an existing eid, human id or name; '$name' or a fresh UUID creates an entity. Exactly one target is required; unsupported predicates are refused, not ignored. For several entities use bundles. Pass q or bundles, never both.

q.description: one entity patch: '.entity.eid=<id> .book.pages=500' or '<id> .book.pages=500'; quote a value with spaces, .doc.title="two words"; schema-typed values, null clears (also quoted null), !component removes; $name or a fresh UUID creates an entity

bundles.description: bundles to apply together: each needs entity: {eid}, '$name' for a new entity or the eid or name of an existing one (an edge needs none: its ends make its eid), and the component fields to write; omitted fields stay unchanged

check.description: true to validate without keeping the proposed changes and return what would have been written; default false

annotations.title: Apply a query patch or a batch of bundles

name: graph_query
title: Query entities
description: Find stored records (entities) by filtering on their named groups of fields (components) and their properties. Returns bundles: JSON objects with entity: {eid} and the record’s component objects. A bundle carries the components the query names, by a filter on one ('.recipe', '.doc.title~=cake') or by asking for one without filtering on it ('?doc'), and no other: name each component you will read, or add * for all of them. A query that names no component ('.entity.eid=T-12', a bare search word) answers whole. Bare words search the text, best match first (a record whose title is exactly the words before all), and answer the best 20 unless .limit says how many; naming no component, each record also carries a query-only hit (its id, the human id such as T-12 where it has one, then kind, title, and a snippet with \u0001 and \u0002 around the matched words), and the answer's text says each as that one line. graph_show returns one entity whole. Answers showing doc.body carry its SHA-256 at $was.doc.body, ready to pass back with a body replacement through graph_apply. A query string selects the records: '.task.status=open&.filed.priority<3'. It is made of filters written as .component.property=value, joined with &, with lists (a,b), ranges (1..9), != for not equal, ~= for text containing a value, < or > comparisons, '.component' for present and '!component' for absent ('?component' filters nothing: it rides beside a filter, as in '.recipe&?doc'), and no spaces around an operator. A property is always named with its component, and only a property holds a value: '.topic.name~=moss', never '.topic~=moss'. A bare word searches all indexed text. Directives go in the same string: .order= names a property ('.order=-created.at', where - sorts descending) or a ranking (hot), .limit=20 caps the answer, and .refs=<id> selects everything that references an entity. filters, if passed, each narrow the whole of q. Documentation: https://yaks.app/docs/querying.

q.description: query filters, e.g. .task.status=open&.filed.priority<3; graph_schema lists the valid components and properties

filters.description: extra filters, each narrowing the whole of q

limit.description: return at most this many entities

name: graph_show
title: Show entities
description: Read one or more stored records (entities) by their unique string id (eid), each returned whole as its own bundle: a JSON object with entity: {eid} and every named group of fields (component) it has. When a bundle shows doc.body, $was.doc.body carries its SHA-256 read token; pass it back on a graph_apply bundle to refuse a concurrent body change (yak graph show prints was:). Only the entities asked for come back, and an id that names nothing is said after them by a line naming it (a call whose ids all name nothing is refused); what references one is a query of its own, graph_query with .refs=<id>, and a relationship is an edge entity found the same way. This is lookup by identity, not search: pass eids, or the names entities are addressed by where this store keeps names (an eid wins over a name spelled the same way).

ids.description: the eids or names of the entities to read

name: graph_schema
title: Read the schema
description: Read this store’s vocabulary (schema): each component is a named group of fields attached to an entity, a stored record; its properties are those fields. Returns markdown to read and, as structured content, one JSON Schema document with each component’s entry under $defs, the same shape as a vocab.json. It answers at one of three levels of detail. With no arguments: the index, every component with its meaning and each property’s type. With component (one name or several): that component in full, as declared, with each property’s type and meaning, which properties are server-owned or unique, what it references, and an example value; the markdown adds what references it and an example bundle that writes it. With kind: the definition of a display category such as task, plus index entries for the components it is displayed with. If both kind and component are passed, kind selects the answer. The index says what exists; a component in full is enough to write it. Documentation: https://yaks.app/docs/components.

component.description: a component name, to read it in full; several at once as an array of names, such as ["task", "doc"]

kind.description: a display category declared by the schema, such as task; returns its definition and associated components

name: search
title: Search text
description: Search indexed text by words and, where an embedding index is configured, by meaning. Results are ranked compact bundles: entity gives the eid; query-only hit gives the id to name it by (its human id, such as T-12, where it has one), the title, kind, excerpt and source (text, meaning or both). In a text excerpt, \u0001 and \u0002 mark the start and end of matched words. Use graph_show to read an entity whole. Documentation: https://yaks.app/docs/querying.

limit.description: return at most this many entities

name: comment_new
title: Comment on an entity
description: Create a comment on an entity: doc{body} holds the markdown and comment{target, reply_to} links to its thread and, optionally, the comment it answers. Attributed to the caller. Omit reply_to to start a branch. Returns the applied bundles.

target.description: the entity the comment is about; pass its id or registered name

reply_to.description: the comment this answers on the target thread; omit to start a branch

name: effect_check
title: Check effect runs
description: Check recorded background actions (effects), such as sending mail after a transaction commits. Reports runs marked failed after exhausting their attempts, runs waiting for a handler no plugin declares any more, and runs still pending past their due time by more than the server’s threshold (10 minutes by default). An overdue run can indicate that no process is running them, even while graph writes succeed. Does not retry or mark runs failed itself; with no effect records supported by the schema, reports no findings. Takes no arguments. Returns a report in content.body, with warning or failure findings when present; it does not repair the records or configuration.

name: effect_retry
title: Retry failed effect runs
description:
Put failed effect runs back to pending with a fresh attempt allowance, so the pool works them again through its ordinary path: attempts, backoff and leases as for a new run. If the cause is fixed they finish; if not they fail again and the check reports them again. Takes a handler name or a single run. Touches only failed runs of a handler some plugin declares, and says how many.

  yak effect retry send_receipt

of.description: a handler name (all its failed runs) or one run's id

name: effect_drop
title: Drop failed effect runs
description:
Delete effect runs whose work no one owes any more, so the check stops reporting them: failed runs, and pending runs whose handler no plugin declares any more. Takes a handler name or a single run, and says how many.

  yak effect drop session_run

of.description: a handler name (all its failed runs) or one run's id

name: history
title: Read an entity’s history
description: List every committed transaction that touched one entity, newest first. Each is returned as the patch it applied (the named groups of fields it wrote, or $delete if it deleted the record) stamped with who wrote it, when, and through which tool or process. The journal is written inside the same transaction as the batch, so this gives attribution and a diff without a version table. It covers changes made since this graph started journaling.

entity.description: record whose history to read: human-readable id, registered name, or unique entity id (eid)

limit.description: return at most this many transactions, counting back from the newest

name: task_new
title: Create a task
description: Create a task: a stored record with task{} and doc{title, body} field groups. It is open because it has neither a completed nor a cancelled mark. Pass a project, priority, assignee or domain and it gets a filed{} group holding those filing fields too. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed.

title.description: what to do, in one line

body.description: what is being asked for, plus pointers to the details, as markdown

project.description: the project to file it under; pass its id or registered name

priority.description: queue order; lower is more urgent

assignee.description: id or registered name of the person or agent whose queue it goes in

check.description: rehearse the write and roll it back, returning the resolved task without saving it

name: task_list
title: List tasks
description: List the tasks a query selects, as bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and component fields. `.task` is always part of the query and narrows the whole of yours; with no query, `.task.status=open` is used. Use filters of the form .component.property=value joined with &: `.task.status=done`, `.filed.project=P-19`, `.filed.priority<3`, or a bare word to match text.

name: task_update
title: Update a task
description: Change a task’s status, title, body or filing. `status` is not a stored field: done adds the completed mark and removes the cancelled one, cancelled does the reverse, and open removes both. Anything left out is unchanged. With body, pass was from $was.doc.body on task_list or graph_show to refuse a concurrent body change; without was the replacement is blind. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed.

task.description: the task to change; pass its id or registered name

status.description: the new status: open, done or cancelled

was.description: the SHA-256 at $was.doc.body returned by task_list or graph_show (was: in yak graph show); when supplied with body, refuse if the body moved since that read

project.description: the project to file it under; pass its id or registered name

priority.description: queue order; lower is more urgent

assignee.description: id or registered name of the person or agent whose queue it goes in

name: decision_new
title: Ask a decision
description: Ask a question as a task wearing decision{question, choices, recommended}. Give two to four labelled choices with descriptions and recommend one by label. Assign it to the person being asked. Work that requires it waits until it is answered; otherwise it is eventual. Returns applied bundles.

choices.description: Two to four choices, each a label and a line saying what it means.

project.description: the project to file it under; pass its id or registered name

priority.description: queue order; lower is more urgent

assignee.description: id or registered name of the person or agent whose queue it goes in

name: decision_answer
title: Answer a decision
description: Answer with a listed choice’s label or your own words. Records decided{choice} attributed to the caller, completes the task, and releases work requiring it. An answered or cancelled decision refuses another answer. Returns applied bundles.

decision.description: The decision task to answer; its id or registered name.

choice.description: A listed label or a custom answer.

name: board_check
title: Check board queries
description: Check saved board queries (filters defining which records a board displays) against the store’s vocabulary, its schema of components and fields. A board is its query, so a query naming removed components or invalid fields can leave work missing from the board; this check reports why it no longer resolves. Takes no arguments. Returns a report in content.body, with warning or failure findings when present; it does not repair the records or configuration.

name: project_check
title: Check project coverage
description: Report records that should belong to a project but do not. A record is checked if it has a component marked governed: true in the schema, such as task or design. It is covered if filed directly under a project or reached through containment relationships from a project or a filed record. The server chooses which relationships mean containment; the default is contains. Uncovered work can be missed by project-based reports. Takes no arguments. Returns a report in content.body, with warning or failure findings when present; it does not repair the records or configuration.

name: design_new
title: Propose a design
description: Write a proposed change down as a stored record with named field groups: design{}, doc{title, body} and proposed{}. Who proposed it and when are stamped from the caller, never passed as arguments. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed.

title.description: what the design proposes, in one line

project.description: the project to file it under; pass its id or registered name

name: design_decide
title: Decide a design
description: Record the decision on a proposed design: approved or declined. The decider is the caller, stamped from the caller’s identity, so a decision an agent makes is recorded as the agent’s, and as an owner’s only when the owner is calling. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed.

design.description: id or registered name of the design proposal to decide

verdict.description: decision to record: approved (default) or declined

name: claim_take
title: Claim an entity
description: Reserve a stored record (entity) for an agent work session so another session cannot claim it. This reservation is a claim or lease: writing one over another session’s claim fails the whole batch, so release first. The same session claiming again is a no-op refresh. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed.

target.description: the entity to claim; any entity at all; pass its id or registered name

session.description: the session that holds the claim (default: the caller’s session); pass its id or registered name

name: claim_release
title: Release a claim
description: Remove the reservation (claim) held by an agent work session on a stored record (entity). Deliberately unguarded: releasing is how a claim is handed over, and a dead session’s claims are released by whichever process notices first. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed.

target.description: the entity whose claim to release; pass its id or registered name

name: session_context
title: Read a session’s context
description: At the start of an agent work session, find or create its stored session record. Pass the id assigned by the harness (the program hosting the agent), or a hook containing session_id. When the hook also gives cwd and the session wears no persona, records the persona of the checkout holding that directory as the one it wears. Returns the session record changes and text in content.body naming the session and records it holds claims (work reservations) on, for the harness to inject. For a UserPromptSubmit hook, instead returns one short timing line from its local transcript_path, without changing the session or claims; an unreadable transcript returns no context. No sent-time field is supplied by the hook: a matching queued submission supplies its timestamp, otherwise the line labels hook time as observed. An explicit session argument takes precedence over the hook for other events. With no session id, including a malformed hook without an explicit id, returns nothing and makes no changes.

session.description: session id assigned by the harness (the program hosting the agent), or an existing session’s human-readable id or unique entity id; takes precedence over hook

hook.description: lifecycle event encoded as a JSON string containing hook_event_name and session_id (UserPromptSubmit also supplies transcript_path, prompt and optionally prompt_id), and optionally cwd, the directory the session started in; the CLI accepts - to read this JSON from stdin, but MCP callers pass the JSON string itself

actor.description: id or name of the persistent identity this session acts as, retained when the agent clears its conversation

name: session_wrap
title: Wrap up a session
description: At the end of an agent work session, save the optional brief (its own account of what it did) and release every claim, or work reservation, it still holds, except a task a managed run is parked on (one still waiting on a dependency, which wakes the run when it finishes). Pass a session id or a hook containing session_id. Returns bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and field groups) for the brief and claim removals. If the session does not exist or no id is supplied, returns nothing and makes no changes.

session.description: session id assigned by the harness (the program hosting the agent), or an existing session’s human-readable id or unique entity id; takes precedence over hook

hook.description: lifecycle event encoded as a JSON string containing hook_event_name and session_id (UserPromptSubmit also supplies transcript_path, prompt and optionally prompt_id), and optionally cwd, the directory the session started in; the CLI accepts - to read this JSON from stdin, but MCP callers pass the JSON string itself

brief.description: what this session did, in its own words

name: session_brief
title: Record a session’s brief
description: Save an agent work session’s brief: its own account of what it did. Replaces any previous brief; creates a session record if a named transcript does not exist. Pass text; session takes precedence over a hook containing session_id, then defaults to the caller’s session. Returns the session id and written fields as a JSON bundle. This stores the brief but does not itself inject it into another session.

session.description: session id assigned by the harness (the program hosting the agent), or an existing session’s human-readable id or unique entity id; takes precedence over hook

hook.description: lifecycle event encoded as a JSON string containing hook_event_name and session_id (UserPromptSubmit also supplies transcript_path, prompt and optionally prompt_id), and optionally cwd, the directory the session started in; the CLI accepts - to read this JSON from stdin, but MCP callers pass the JSON string itself

name: hooks_install
title: Install the lifecycle hooks
description: Write SessionStart, SubagentStart, UserPromptSubmit and SessionEnd hooks (commands run when an agent session or subagent starts, receives a prompt or ends) into a Claude-compatible harness settings file, so every session starts by reading its context back (session_context) and ends by wrapping up (session_wrap), each prompt receives a short timing line from its local transcript, a PreToolUse HTTP hook that posts each MCP tool call to the server's hook door before it runs, so the MCP door writes as the session or subagent making it, and a PostToolUse HTTP hook that posts each tool call to the same door, where the session hears what it is owed and its subagents hear nothing. The turns in between are read from the harness's own transcript file by the package's duty. Replaces an earlier install, including the turn hooks an older one wrote, and leaves every other entry in the file alone. Writes to the machine the tool runs on. Returns a text confirmation naming the settings path. Pass remove: true to uninstall just these hooks.

yak.description: the path to the yak command on this machine

server.description: the yak serve whose hook door the PostToolUse hook posts to (default http://localhost:5173)

remove.description: remove the entries instead of writing them

name: claim_check
title: Check for stale claims
description: Check for work reservations (claims) on records (entities) whose agent session is over: a holder this graph has no session entity for, or one whose session stopped or failed. Otherwise the board reports somebody working on what nobody is working on. Takes no arguments. Returns a report in content.body, with warning or failure findings when present; it does not repair the records or configuration.

name: session_check
title: Check for stalled sessions
description: Reconcile sessions whose process exited or whose fully imported outside transcript ended, then report sessions still waiting on a turn or answer past the server’s stall threshold (two hours by default). An uncertain ending stays a warning. Takes no arguments. Returns the report in content.body.

name: visualize_anatomy
title: Read the platform's anatomy
description: Read this host's composed platform anatomy: packages, roles, facets, vocabulary, tools, commands, rules, effects, routes, views, kits, themes, skills and secret names. Declaration, loading and binding are separate facts; an unobserved category is not globally absent. Returns the same filtered JSON snapshot as /visualize/anatomy, with coverage and node-only selection counts. Edges are kept only between included nodes. This reads no entity data or secret values and does not force lazy facets to load.

group.description: one anatomy group; omitted means every group

search.description: plain-text anatomy search, not a graph query

id.description: one exact anatomy part id, not a stored entity id

limit.description: maximum nodes shown; selection reports total, matching and shown counts with a truncation flag

name: visualize_activity
title: Capture causal platform activity
description: Capture bounded causal activity from this tool host's process-local trace channel: apply phases, rules, queries, gets, effects, requests and fanout. Returns the same JSON capture DTO as /visualize/activity: epoch, events with sequence and causal span ids, a known omitted record count (gap) and explicit process-local coverage. Recording is subscriber-only; no earlier idle work is reconstructed and another process using the same store is not covered. Uses the existing trace stream, never a second measurement stream. Events carry fixed operation names, durations and counts, never query text, entity contents, payloads or secret values. A zero duration is valid.

limit.description: maximum retained activity events, including start and end events

wait.description: milliseconds to keep this capture subscribed; zero reads only available history

name: session_spawn
title: Start an agent on a task
description: Start an agent on a task. Creates a session record for the run, an initial log entry naming the provider (agent runner), model and reasoning effort, and a claim reserving the task for that session; committing that starts the agent, so a task another session already holds refuses the whole request. With wait, returns how the run ended (its brief or final output, and its exit code when recorded) instead of the session id. Returns text in content.body. A wait timeout reports that the run is still running and does not kill it.

task.description: the task to hand to the agent, which the session claims; pass its id or registered name

provider.description: id or registered name of the provider (agent runner); it must use command-line transport

model.description: id or registered name of the model the run uses; optional

persona.description: the persona to carry, by id or name (default: the checkout's persona)

effort.description: the reasoning effort, where the model accepts such a setting

instruction.description: additional instructions beside the task body, which is the agent’s spec

wait.description: block until the run is over and return how it ended

timeout.description: how long to wait: 45m, 2h, or bare seconds (default 30m)

annotations.title: Start an agent on a task

name: session_stop
title: Stop a managed session
description: Stop a session. A native transcript admits no further steps and reads stopped; an already admitted step may finish. A managed process receives SIGTERM and then SIGKILL if needed. Use session wait to see when it has ended. Returns text in content.body.

session.description: the session to stop; pass its id or registered name

name: session_wait
title: Wait for a session to end
description: Wait for a session to end, then return its brief (or final output) and exit code when recorded, as text in content.body. A session still running when the timeout passes is reported as still running, never killed.

session.description: the session to wait on; pass its id or registered name

timeout.description: how long to wait: 45m, 2h, or bare seconds (default 30m)

annotations.title: Wait for a session to end

name: session_peek
title: Read the end of a session
description: Return the last entries of an agent work session as stored in the graph, plus its current status. Returns at most lines entries (40 by default, 256 maximum), with long entry bodies previewed, as text in content.body; never the provider’s own log file.

session.description: the session to read; pass its id or registered name

lines.description: how many entries to return, newest last (default 40)

annotations.title: Read the end of a session

name: persona_read
title: Read a persona
description: Read a persona (a named set of agent instructions) by id or name. Returns one markdown document: its own instruction text, then the full text of every document it includes, then one line naming each document it only references. This is the text an agent is given; where it goes (a file, a repository, a spawned agent’s system prompt) is up to the caller.

persona.description: the persona’s unique entity id (eid), human-readable id, registered name, or exact title

name: persona_sync
title: Write the persona files
description: Write each project’s personas into its checkout, where a harness started there reads them: the persona the project contains as .tasks/AGENTS.md (a repository’s CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md link to it), and every other persona whose home is the project as .tasks/personas/<name>.md (a .claude/agents/<name>.md links to one). Only a file whose text moved is written; the file of a renamed or deleted persona is removed; a file edited by hand while the graph also moved is left alone and reported. Returns one line per file it wrote, removed or left.

check.description: write nothing: report the files that would change

name: memory_save
title: Save a memory
description: Save what somebody said, in their own words, as a memory. Words the graph already holds are marked where they are, never copied: pass on to name the entity holding them (a session entry, a comment, a doc), or pass said with feedback naming who said them, and the earliest entity that person wrote holding those words verbatim is marked. Words it cannot place become a new entity, the sentence itself and never your summary of it. A mark never edits the words, and nothing needs approving. context is a line or two somebody will need to read it weeks later. scope names the project it belongs to; leave it out when creating a principle that applies everywhere (when patching, omission keeps the existing scope). feedback names who gave the correction, when the words are one. Pass id to patch an existing memory instead: anything left out is unchanged, and replacing the words requires was, the string at $was.doc.body that memory_recall returns beside them, so a memory another writer changed since you read it is refused whole rather than overwritten; the words of a comment, an entry or anything else a memory marks are what happened there and are never replaced. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed; a mark's is the entity it marked. Creating a memory requires said or on; omit id to create one.

said.description: the words the person used, as they used them

on.description: the entity already holding the words, to mark instead of copying them: a session entry, a comment, a doc; said, if passed too, must be in its text

title.description: the index line a recall shows first, for a new memory; a mark leaves the entity's own text alone

context.description: what was being discussed, in two lines; never a restatement of what was said

scope.description: project id or name; omit on creation for a memory that applies everywhere, or on a patch to keep the current scope

feedback.description: the correcting person’s id or name, or an empty string if unknown; either marks the memory as feedback

about.description: the app the words were said about, by slug

id.description: existing memory’s id or registered name to patch; omit to create a memory

was.description: the string at $was.doc.body on the memory returned by memory_recall; required when replacing existing words

name: memory_recall
title: Recall memories
description: Find saved memories by what they are about. Where the server has a vector index, said ranks them by meaning, closest first, whether or not they share its words; without one, said selects the memories containing all its words, newest first. near is an entity id or name whose meaning ranks the results instead, and said then selects by its words. With neither said nor near, returns the newest memories. Results are bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and component fields), each whole: the words wherever the memory marks them (a doc's body, a session entry's content) and its context, never snippets. Each carries $was.doc.body, the string to pass as memory_save’s was when replacing those words. Optional ids, scope and feedback narrow the results; limit defaults to 8.

said.description: what the memory is about, in a few words: ranked by meaning where this server has a vector index, otherwise matched as text terms the memory must all contain

near.description: entity id or name whose meaning ranks the results, when this server has a vector index; said then selects by its words

scope.description: project id or registered name; return only memories filed under it

feedback.description: only memories recording a correction somebody gave

name: memory_source
title: Where somebody said these words
description: Where a person said these words: the earliest entity they wrote whose text holds them verbatim (the session entry they typed, a comment, a doc), whole. The same words in anybody else's text are a quote of them and never count. Use it on words quoted from somebody to find where they said them, then mark that entity with memory_save's on. Returns bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and component fields). Refuses where nothing that person wrote holds the words.

said.description: the words, exactly as they were written; line breaks and runs of spaces do not count

by.description: who said them: their id or registered name

name: memory_around
title: Read the transcript around an entry
description: The transcript around a session entry, like grep -C: up to before entries ahead of it, the entry itself, and up to after entries behind it, in transcript order. Use it on a memory marked on an entry to see what was being said when the words were said. Entries of every kind count: what a person typed, the model's replies, tool calls and their results. Returns bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and component fields), each whole. Refuses an entity that is no transcript entry.

id.description: the memory, or any entity, to read around: its id or registered name

before.description: how many entries ahead of it (default 3)

annotations.title: Read the transcript around an entry

name: memory_target
title: What an entity is aimed at
description: What an entity is aimed at: the entity each of its components' target names (a comment's target, or any other component that has one), whole, so you see what it is: a task, a doc, a component's definition (_comp), the comment it replies to. Use it on a memory marked on a comment to see what the comment was about. Returns bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and component fields). Refuses an entity aimed at nothing.

id.description: the memory, or any entity, to read around: its id or registered name

annotations.title: What an entity is aimed at

name: memory_thread
title: Read the discussion an entity is in
description: The discussion an entity is part of: what its comments are ultimately about (a comment's target, followed up past every comment it replies to), then every comment on that and every reply below them, oldest first. Given something no comment is aimed at, it answers that entity alone. Returns bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and component fields), each whole.

id.description: the memory, or any entity, to read around: its id or registered name

annotations.title: Read the discussion an entity is in

name: memory_session
title: Where something happened
description: Where something happened: the session it was written in (a transcript entry's session, or the session anything else was written through), then what that session worked on or holds a claim on, its tasks. Returns bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and component fields), each whole. Refuses an entity no session wrote.

id.description: the memory, or any entity, to read around: its id or registered name

name: topic_read
title: Read a topic as a session's context
description: Read a topic as the context a session opened on it is given (session_new with topic): one markdown document with the topics that contain it, its cover, its contents and their $was token, everything it holds in full (a long body cut, with the id to read the rest), the topics below it as an outline, and what to understand first, what is related and its sources, one line each. Returns text in content.body.

annotations.title: Read a topic as a session's context

name: topic_new
title: Make a topic
description: Make a topic, where no existing topic fits; a project is already its own topic. name is what it is called, as plain and general as the subject is ("testing", "ui components", "naming"), never a phrase about one point; body is its cover, a line or two saying what belongs under it, never a point anybody made. It belongs to whatever contains it, so its name and cover never say the project: put one about a project under the project with topic_add. One name is one topic: a name that is taken is refused with the topic that has it, to use instead, and so is a name whose words hold another topic's or are held by them ("economic market design" beside "market design"). Returns the applied bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and components); the topic's id is its entity.eid.

name.description: what the topic is called, a few plain words

body.description: a line or two saying what belongs under it

name: topic_find
title: Find topics
description: Find existing topics: those whose name, title or cover holds each word in said, as the start of a word or by its stem ("data modeling" finds "data model", "tests" finds "testing"), ranked by meaning to the entity near names when the server has a vector index, or, given neither, the topics in order of name. Use it to find what is known about a subject (graph_show on a topic lists what it holds), before putting something you wrote under its topic (topic_add), and before making a topic, with near set to what you are filing under one, so a subject already named is reused rather than named again in other words. Returns bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and components), each whole; limit defaults to 12.

said.description: words the topic's name, title or cover holds, as the start of a word or by its stem

near.description: an entity id or name whose meaning ranks the topics

name: topic_add
title: Add to a topic
description: Put entities under a topic, where whoever reads the topic finds them: a memory, a design, a skill, a package, somebody's words, or a subtopic. Each gets a contains edge from the topic; adding one already there changes nothing, and drop takes them out instead. One entity may sit under several topics. Find the topic first with topic_find, or make one with topic_new; a project is its own topic, so its id or name places things under it. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed.

topic.description: the topic's id or title, or a project's

ids.description: the entities to put under it, by id

drop.description: take them out of the topic instead

name: vector_check
title: Check stored vectors
description: Check embedding configuration and the vector search engine. Reports missing embedding configuration, a missing vector table, an unavailable native scan on shared storage, or mixed model spaces requiring the ordinary vector reader. Takes no arguments and changes no records.

name: builder_build
title: Build now
description: Build bindings with new or changed inputs, independent of floor and staged. Current outputs are untouched unless --rebuild redoes every selected binding, or --outdated redoes bindings under an older definition. Both combine with --only and --limit. Alternate provider, model, template or native input creates a shadow variant.

builder.description: id of the builder to build

provider.description: the provider to ask instead of the configured one

model.description: the model to build with instead of the configured one

template.description: alternate content.body template for a shadow variant

input.description: native request fields merged into sending.input for a shadow variant; --input @input.json reads an object

only.description: build only the bindings whose outer entities these name, and leave the other builds as they are

limit.description: build only the first n bindings, and leave the other builds as they are

rebuild.description: redo every selected binding, even with unchanged inputs and definition

outdated.description: redo selected bindings only when their definition is older; otherwise build only missing or changed inputs

name: builder_supply
title: Supply an existing artifact
description: Answer one binding's slot with an existing artifact, spending nothing. The binding is current until its own inputs change. A staged builder accepts supply; an archived builder does not.

for.description: the first entity in exactly one outer binding

args.description: provenance kept beside the frozen binding on the supplied call

name: builder_choose
title: Choose an output take
description: Make one retained output the take in use for its build and slot, without a call or spending. Other slots stay chosen as they are.

name: mail_show
title: Read a mail message
description: Return one mail message in full: its headers, its body, and one-line summaries of the rest of its thread, with this message marked. The text is returned in content.body alongside the opened mark. Reading marks the caller's subscription to the thread opened, which is why this tool writes where graph_show only reads.

letter.description: the message to read; pass its id or registered name

name: mail_reply
title: Reply to a mail message
description: Write a reply threaded on one message and request that it be sent. It is addressed to the other side of the original (the sender of a received message, or the recipient of one you sent) from the address the original used, with the subject prefixed `Re:`. Replying to a received message archives the caller's subscription to its thread: a thread you have answered is not waiting on you. The configured sender delivers it; a graph with no sender configured records the reply and never sends it. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed. Confirm the recipient and message before requesting delivery; a sent email cannot be recalled.

letter.description: the message being replied to; pass its id or registered name

name: mail_send
title: Send a mail message
description: Create a mail message and request that it be sent. It sends from an address this graph holds, through the graph’s own sender, and never from a person’s own mail account: asked to email someone with nothing here named, use whatever mail tool the person has connected. `to` is an email address or the id of an entity in this graph; an address nobody in the graph has becomes a new `email` entity, so the address book grows as mail is sent. `from` defaults to the email address of the entity it is `about`, such as a project’s own, so the answer comes back to that entity; otherwise to the caller’s own email address. Without a configured sender, the message is recorded but not sent. A configured sender delivers it asynchronously and writes `delivered` or `bounced` onto the message. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed. Confirm the recipient and message before requesting delivery; a sent email cannot be recalled. The initial result is not a delivery receipt; read the message again to check its outcome.

to.description: an email address, or the id of the entity it is for

from.description: the address it is sent from (default: the address of what it is about, else the caller’s own)

about.description: the entity this message is about, so the correspondence is attached to it; pass its id or registered name

name: mail_check
title: Check the mail
description: Check that every received mail message has a sender. Also reports incomplete configuration for a sender this server has configured. A message with a Message-ID but no `from` can never be answered, since a reply has no address to go to. Takes no arguments. Returns a report in content.body, with warning or failure findings when present; it does not repair the records or configuration.

name: cites_check
title: Check citations
description: Report citations that moved or were never checked. A `cites` edge points to a `file`, to some lines of one (an entity wearing `lines{file, start, end}`), to a symbol, or to any other graph entity. For a file of a repository, its lines or a symbol in it, Git answers in this checkout, which must be of that repository, which commits after `revision.commit` touched the cited place. For anything else, its current content hash is compared with `cites.hash`, recorded when verified; this needs no journal or checkout. A citation nobody checked is unverified, and one without enough evidence is unknown. Scope with `of` (only citations one entity makes) or `path` (only citations of one file of this checkout's repository: the file, lines of it, or a symbol in it). Returns a report in content.body with warning or failure findings. It writes nothing and enforces nothing.

of.description: only the citations this record makes; pass its id or registered name

path.description: only citations of this file of this checkout's repository, lines of it or a symbol in it; the path as Git spells it

name: cites_verify
title: Verify a citation
description: Record that a citation was checked and holds. For a file of a repository, lines of one or a symbol, write the `verified` mark and move its `revision` to this checkout's commit; the checkout must be of that repository. For another entity, write the mark and its current content hash in `cites.hash`, without needing a checkout. Takes the citation edge itself, or an entity, meaning every citation it makes. Returns the citations as written.

cite.description: the citation to mark; pass its id

of.description: a record, meaning every citation it makes

name: land
title: Land the current branch
description: Land the branch the current checkout is on. Fast-forwards it into the base branch (the one the shared checkout has checked out) and pushes if the base has an upstream. If the base has moved, rebases the branch onto it and returns without merging, printing what the rebase pulled in so the caller can re-run its tests and land again; that counts as a failure, because nothing landed. Refuses to land when a file would end up with content no commit on the branch wrote, unless allow-revert names that file. Runs no tests and reads no graph: everything comes from Git, in the checkout assigned to this tool call by the host (the CLI uses its current directory). Returns Git’s output and the landed commit SHA in content.body. No arguments are needed for an ordinary landing.

allow-revert.description: comma-separated paths whose reverted content is intended; they land with a warning

name: code_sync
title: Sync the codebase
description: Read the codebase of the checkout this call runs in into the graph: a package per manifest, a module per TypeScript, JavaScript or Markdown file Git tracks, a symbol per export, and an `imports` link per import. Only files whose Git blob moved since the last sync are read again; a file that is gone has its module and symbols cleared, never deleted, so a path or name that comes back is the same entity. Returns a one-paragraph report of what it read, cleared and how long it took.

full.description: read every file, not only the ones that moved

name: admin_throwaway
title: Sign in as a throwaway test account
description:
Sign this box in as a throwaway test account, <name>@bot.yak.sh. Without a name, a fresh probe-<random> address. The sign-in code is read from the letter in this graph. The current account stays as it was: name the new one per command with --as.

  yak admin throwaway cookbook

name.description: the local part of the address

annotations.title: Sign in as a throwaway test account

name: admin_link
title: Make a standing sign-in link
description:
One URL that signs its holder in as this account until it expires, or --revoke to take one back by its id.

  yak admin throwaway reviewer && yak admin link --days=90 --as=reviewer
  yak admin link --revoke=3f2a --as=reviewer

Requires the website session retained by a code sign-in; browser OAuth sign-ins have none.

revoke.description: a link id to revoke instead

as.description: the owner’s yaks.app connection, matched by whole address or the part before @; list the owner’s connections with connection_list(owner), or yak connection list <owner> (owner id or name), and use a yaks.app entry’s account. Default is your own email, else the oldest connection

name: admin_fee
title: Read or set the platform’s fee
description:
What the platform takes from a sale, in basis points: read it, or set it. The rate is the platform’s, so the selected account must have the platform role.

  yak admin fee --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin fee 250 --as admin@bot.yak.sh

bps.description: the new rate, in whole basis points

as.description: the owner’s yaks.app connection, matched by whole address or the part before @; list the owner’s connections with connection_list(owner), or yak connection list <owner> (owner id or name), and use a yaks.app entry’s account. Default is your own email, else the oldest connection

annotations.title: Read or set the platform’s fee

name: admin_move
title: Rehearse or run the store mover in every yaks.app store
description:
The store mover brings a store's rows into a new shape from its alarm, a batch at a time (workers/yak/mover.ts). This asks every store in turn, the app stores first and the directory last, and prints a line per store and rule as it goes. --rehearse moves each rule's rows inside a transaction the store rolls back, up to twenty batches, and says what it found and moved, any failure, and how long the store took to answer; without it each store is woken to move what it owes, a few a minute, and says where each rule stands. A space or space/app narrows it. The platform’s act, so the selected account must have the platform role.

  yak admin move --rehearse --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin move --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin move ada --rehearse --as admin@bot.yak.sh

pace.description: stores a minute, 0 for each as soon as the last answers (5 for a wake, 0 for a rehearsal)

as.description: the owner’s yaks.app connection, matched by whole address or the part before @; list the owner’s connections with connection_list(owner), or yak connection list <owner> (owner id or name), and use a yaks.app entry’s account. Default is your own email, else the oldest connection

annotations.title: Rehearse or run the store mover in every yaks.app store

name: admin_tunnel
title: A space's tunnel to a machine
description:
The tunnel a space has to a machine, whose server the space's apps reach through the tunnel's gateway (a vpc_services door in their config), at the paths its @yaks/tunnel config opens. With no act, what the tunnel is. connect makes a tunnel, its service to the port given, and the gateway; rotate puts the gateway again, and gives the tunnel a new token where the platform made it; adopt records a tunnel and service made elsewhere with a gateway in front, and is the platform's act. A token answered is kept in this graph's vault as TUNNEL_TOKEN without printing it, where @yaks/tunnel's service reads it. disconnect removes the tunnel.

  yak admin tunnel yak --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin tunnel yak adopt --tunnel <id> --service <id> --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin tunnel ada connect --port 5173

act.description: what to change; nothing reads the tunnel

port.description: connect: the port the machine's server listens on

as.description: the owner’s yaks.app connection, matched by whole address or the part before @; list the owner’s connections with connection_list(owner), or yak connection list <owner> (owner id or name), and use a yaks.app entry’s account. Default is your own email, else the oldest connection

annotations.title: A space's tunnel to a machine

name: admin_delete
title: Close a space for good
description:
Close a space: its apps, their data, and its address. What would go is listed first, the same list the confirmation letter carries to a person whose agent asked.

Requires the website session retained by a code sign-in; browser OAuth sign-ins have none.

as.description: the owner’s yaks.app connection, matched by whole address or the part before @; list the owner’s connections with connection_list(owner), or yak connection list <owner> (owner id or name), and use a yaks.app entry’s account. Default is your own email, else the oldest connection

name: admin_deploys
title: List yaks.app versions and deployments
description: Recent yaks.app uploads and deployments with their commits and live times; ~ marks a commit inferred by time. Migration boundaries survive code rollbacks, and unknown history refuses a rollback. Infrastructure requires the platform admin or the configured person’s own account.

as.description: the owner’s yaks.app connection, matched by whole address or the part before @; list the owner’s connections with connection_list(owner), or yak connection list <owner> (owner id or name), and use a yaks.app entry’s account. Default is your own email, else the oldest connection

name: admin_errors
title: List yaks.app failures by tracker bug
description: Every unresolved tracker bug (not resolved or archived), however old, newest first. No time window by default; since optionally narrows by last seen. Thrown or caught: lifetime count, first and last seen, global bug id, place and message. Then the time to fix of the bugs resolved in the window (a week without since): median and worst, first seen or regressed to resolved; and how long the oldest open bug has been open. Pass resolved to include each resolved bug’s full explanation. Then people's letters to the platform's addresses in the same window: how many, how many have a reply in their thread with median and worst time to answer, and each one still unanswered (archive a letter that needs no answer). Reads the tracker through its signed door using the remote URL and vault reference in tracker.json beside this graph; `admin tail` watches live traffic. Infrastructure requires the platform admin or the configured person’s own account.

resolved.description: include each bug resolved in the window with its full explanation; default only reports time-to-fix totals

since.description: optional duration narrowing bugs by last seen (for example 7d); no time window by default

as.description: the owner’s yaks.app connection, matched by whole address or the part before @; list the owner’s connections with connection_list(owner), or yak connection list <owner> (owner id or name), and use a yaks.app entry’s account. Default is your own email, else the oldest connection

annotations.title: List yaks.app failures by tracker bug

name: admin_rollback
title: Roll yaks.app back to a prior version
description: Emergency rollback, only for a broken build path: code corrections use `yak admin revert`, since main deploys on every push. Defaults to the prior deployed version, refuses data boundaries and uncertain commits, then probes the public doors. Infrastructure requires the platform admin or the configured person’s own account.

as.description: the owner’s yaks.app connection, matched by whole address or the part before @; list the owner’s connections with connection_list(owner), or yak connection list <owner> (owner id or name), and use a yaks.app entry’s account. Default is your own email, else the oldest connection

annotations.title: Roll yaks.app back to a prior version

name: admin_revert
title: Revert a main commit and wait for it to deploy
description: Revert a main commit in a fresh worktree, run deno task check, land and push main, and wait up to 20m for Workers Builds to serve the revert. A failed worktree is kept. Infrastructure requires the platform admin or the configured person’s own account.

as.description: the owner’s yaks.app connection, matched by whole address or the part before @; list the owner’s connections with connection_list(owner), or yak connection list <owner> (owner id or name), and use a yaks.app entry’s account. Default is your own email, else the oldest connection

annotations.title: Revert a main commit and wait for it to deploy

name: admin_gallery
title: Decide, code-review or list a gallery app
description:
As the platform admin, act on a gallery request. code-review records your review of the code of an app somebody else asked into the gallery, which comes to you as a task, and sends the platform’s owner its review request with your verdict and findings. approve and decline answer a request, and list puts a published app in the gallery at once, skipping review: do those only when the platform’s owner asks, and name him with --by. The session is recorded from this call.

  yak admin gallery acme/todo code-review --verdict approve --findings @findings.md --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin gallery jeff/housebook approve --by jeff@yak.sh --as admin@bot.yak.sh
  yak admin gallery yourname/garden list --by jeff@yak.sh --as admin@bot.yak.sh

decision.description: approve or decline answers a request (gallery_review); list puts the app in the gallery now, with no request and no review (app_set gallery: true, review: false); code-review records your code review and sends the request on (gallery_code_review)

verdict.description: with code-review: whether the code should be listed

findings.description: with code-review: what the review found, as text or @file

by.description: who the decision is recorded as: the platform owner’s address when he asked for it; default the calling agent’s project

reason.description: why a request was approved or declined

as.description: the owner’s yaks.app connection, matched by whole address or the part before @; list the owner’s connections with connection_list(owner), or yak connection list <owner> (owner id or name), and use a yaks.app entry’s account. Default is your own email, else the oldest connection

annotations.title: Decide, code-review or list a gallery app

name: connection_need
title: Say an app needs a connection
description: Say that an app needs an outside service: an integration by name, and the scopes it asks for. It makes a connection with no credential, owned by a space or a person, which shows them what to connect; no key or token ever passes through this tool. For a service with no built integration, name it and give the hosts its key may be sent to, and a custom integration is made for it, owned by the asking space; give it instructions too, markdown for a person and their agent saying how to get the key (where to sign up, which page issues it, what to paste), and a title, tagline and site. Its owner asking again with any of those changes them; its hosts never change. With each, every person who uses the app connects their own instead, and the owner connects nothing. An app that already uses a connection through that integration is answered with it. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components written, followed by the integration the connection goes through, its instructions among it, to walk the person through getting the key.

app.description: the app that needs it, by id or name

owner.description: the space or person who will connect it, by id or name

scopes.description: what the app asks for; omit for the integration's own

hosts.description: for a custom key only: the hosts it may be sent to

each.description: each person who uses the app connects their own account, rather than the owner connecting one for everyone. The host draws the Connect button for them, each person's connection shows in their own dashboard, and only they call out through it

binding.description: the name the app's code reads it by (env.NAME); omit for the integration's name in capitals

direct.description: hand the app's code the key itself rather than a sentinel, for a key it must sign with; only for a pasted key

instructions.description: for a custom integration: how a person gets its key, in markdown, written for them and the agent helping them

title.description: for a custom integration: what a person calls the service, as its maker writes it

tagline.description: for a custom integration: one line saying what the service is

site.description: for a custom integration: the service's https address on the web

annotations.title: Say an app needs a connection

name: connection_list
title: List connections
description: The connections a space or a person owns, each with its integration, account, scopes and status (needed, connected or broken), the links from each app that uses one, and the integrations they go through, with each one's instructions for getting its key. A handle is shown where a credential is kept; the credential itself never is. Returns bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and component fields.

owner.description: the space or person, by id or name

name: session_list
title: List sessions
description: List every agent work-session record in the connected graph, as bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and their named groups of fields (components). Takes no arguments; includes sessions regardless of their status.

name: conversation_projects
description: Identify the trusted human caller and list active projects.

name: conversation_start
description: Start a native project conversation without waiting for a reply.

project.description: The active project to talk with.

name: conversation_send
description: Send exact human words to an owned project conversation without waiting.

project.description: The active project to talk with.

name: conversation_read
description: Read a bounded current transcript page, including progressive assistant replies. Poll again to receive revisions to the same message id.

project.description: The active project to talk with.

before.description: Read older entries strictly before this entry sequence. Omit to poll the current tail.

name: conversation_recent
description: List this caller’s recent project conversations.

project.description: The active project to talk with.

name: conversation_inbox
description: Read the trusted human caller’s inbox, using shared inbox policy.

name: session_home
description: Change a session default workspace without moving files, commands or permissions. Omitting cwd clears the previous directory.

cwd.description: Absolute command directory in the workspace filesystem.

name: spend_show
title: Show where the tokens went
description: Report where the model requests of a span of days went, from the tallies the duty keeps: each plan limit against its pace, then the parts of the context, sessions, tasks, models and large entries that cost most, by dollars. Reads tallies only; changes nothing.

since.description: the first UTC day, `2026-10-13` (default: the day the Claude plan's week began, else six days ago)

top.description: how many rows each ranking shows (default 10)
